dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product shows things that are looked at rather than read: a picture in an article, a chart in a report, a diagram, a preview of what a setting will produce, a sample of a template, a specimen of a color or a shape. It sets each apart the same way — on a stage of its own, most inside a quiet frame, a photograph without one — with a line of text that says what is shown; some have a title and a control or two above the stage (which period, which variant), and some have what they were made from, the data or the code, joined beneath.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Everything a figure reads: the frame's corners and, for each look (outlined, filled, plain), its fill; the outlined look's edge; the color the stage hands its content; the stage's padding; the header's paddings and the gap between the title and the actions; the title's text style and color; the caption's text style, color and distance from the frame; the ground pattern a stage may draw behind its content (its color, the spacing of its lines and dots, their width, the side of a checkerboard square, and how much of the centre a fading grid leaves clear); the line between the frame's parts, the choice between that line and space, and the space an attachment keeps when the choice is space.
rules: A figure shows one thing to look at and says what it is: a picture, a chart, a diagram, a preview, a specimen, a live example. Content a person reads through is prose; a group of related content and actions is a card; a notice is a callout.
The stage holds the product's content and nothing of the figure's: the figure never styles, mirrors, crops or operates what is shown. Controls inside a live example keep working.
The title is above, inside the frame; the caption is below, outside it. There is no placement setting: text above the stage is the title.
Every figure has a name for assistive technology: the title, or the caption, or label where neither is drawn. A picture still needs its own alternative text; a caption is not one.
Outlined is the default. Use filled where an edge would add a line to a page that already has many. Use plain for a picture that needs no frame: it draws no fill, no edge, no padding and no line.
The actions in the header are the product's own controls (icon-only Buttons, tabs, a select). The figure lays them out and does nothing else: what they change in the stage is the product's.

The attachment is the product's block joined under the stage (the code of an example, the data of a chart). Under the divider choice it is flush and the line is the figure's; give it in a form without corners and an edge of its own.

A ground pattern behind what is shown is the figure's pattern prop — grid, dots, grid-fade or checkerboard — never one drawn by hand around the stage. It is decoration: quiet in every scheme, behind the content, gone in forced colors and in the plain look. Use a checkerboard where what is shown may be transparent; leave it none where the content is a picture that fills the stage.

Numbering (Figure 3), a status such as do and don't, an aspect ratio and a grid of figures are not the figure's: they are the product's text, a tag in the caption, the media's own box and the product's layout.
Restyle through these tokens in a layer; never draw a framed stage by hand.

shape.$description: The frame's corners, and in the plain look the stage's own: the step of a card and of a callout, so a figure reads as one of the page's blocks. What is shown is clipped to them.

color.$description: The fill of the outlined look, inside the one hairline: the surface itself, the fill an outlined card has. A stage is a known surface, so that what is shown on it has the contrast its own tokens were held to.
The fill of the filled look: a quiet step of the surface ladder, which sets the stage apart by tone and draws no edge.
The plain look has no fill: the surface the figure sits on shows through, and what is shown is its own frame.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: This variant has no fill; the surface behind shows through.

color.$description: The edge of the outlined look: the one hairline, the color a divider and an outlined card draw theirs in. Decorative. It keeps its own token so that a system can draw this edge apart from its dividers.

width.$description: The width of the outlined look's edge, drawn inside the frame's size.

color.$description: The color the outlined and the filled looks hand to what is in the stage, as the platform's inherited foreground: the content color of both fills. The plain look hands nothing: its content takes the color of the surface the figure sits on.

padding-block.$description: Above and below what is shown, while the figure is inset and has a frame: room enough that a specimen's focus ring, shadow and state layer are not cut by the frame, and that a small specimen does not look pressed between two lines.

padding-inline.$description: Before and after what is shown, while the figure is inset and has a frame.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product sets some of the things it shows on a ground that says what kind of surface they stand on — a component on a layout grid in its documentation, a drawing on a dot grid in its editor, a picture that may be transparent on a checkerboard in its asset library — and others on the plain fill; it chooses the pattern per figure and draws every pattern in one quiet color at one rhythm.

color.$description: The lines, the dots and every second checkerboard square of the ground pattern. The highest step of the surface ladder: a step from both fills, so the pattern is seen on the outlined and the filled looks in every scheme, and one that a raised contrast level leaves as it is, so the decoration never grows louder than the content it stands behind. Content in on-surface is held at 4.5:1 against it, as against every surface role.

spacing.$description: The distance between two lines of the grid and between two dots, in both directions: a step of the spacing scale, so that a specimen on the grid can be read against it.

line-thickness.$description: The width of a line of the grid: the one hairline.

dot-size.$description: The diameter of a dot of the dot grid: three strokes, so that a dot in the pattern's quiet color still reads as a point, where one a hairline or two across would be a speck.

checkerboard-size.$description: The side of one checkerboard square: small against what is shown, so a transparent part of a picture reads as transparent rather than as a pattern of its own.

clear-extent.$description: The grid-fade pattern: the share of the way from the stage's centre to its corners that the grid leaves clear. From there the grid grows to full strength at the corners, so that a specimen at the centre stands on the plain fill and the grid frames it.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: A proportion of the stage's own box; no dial scales it.

padding-block.$description: Above and below the header's row.

padding-inline.$description: Before the title, and after it where there are no actions.

padding-inline-end-with-actions.$description: After the actions: tighter than after text, because a control's own shape already holds its content away from the edge. The callout makes the same distinction for its close button.

gap.$description: Between the title and the actions, between two actions, and between the title and a row of actions that moved below it.

typescale.$description: The title: the interface's text size at the heading's weight, the style a callout's title has. It is the label of what is shown, never a heading by itself.
The caption: secondary text, one body role below the interface's, the style prose gives its small print. A caption is a sentence, so it is a body style and not a label's.

color.$description: The caption's color: secondary content. It is drawn outside the frame, on the surface the figure sits on, where this role is held against every surface.

gap.$description: Between the frame and the caption below it; in the plain look also between the title and the stage.

color.$description: The line between the header and the stage and between the stage and the attachment, while separation is divider: the one hairline. It keeps its own token so that a system can draw it apart from the frame's edge.

gap.$description: While separation is gap: the space the attachment keeps from the stage above it and from the frame's inline and bottom edges, in place of the line. In the plain look, the space between the stage and the attachment.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product whose manner is space rather than lines still joins the code of an example to its stage, and chooses how far apart the two stand.

separation.$description: How the parts inside the frame — the header, the stage, the attachment — are told apart. divider: a line of divider.thickness in divider.color between them, the attachment flush with the frame. gap: no line; the attachment stands attachment.gap inside the frame with its own shape. Follows the system's choice; a figure's separation prop overrides it (FIG-12). The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product rules its tables and its figures' parts with a line while its joined buttons stand apart, or parts everything by space: the system-wide choice gives the common answer, and the figure must be able to leave it, because a line under a stage and a line inside a filled control are not the same decision.
